newsitem.title: ITALY: More indictments sought in Italian serial murders.
newsitem.headline: More indictments sought in Italian serial murders.

text.p: An Italian prosecutor sought murder indictments on Tuesday against three men he says took part in a series of double killings known as the "Monster of Florence" murders.
It was the latest twist in a sensational serial murder case that has gripped Italy for decades.
Eight double killings were committed in the Florence area between 1968 and 1985. Most of the victims were young couples and many of the killings involved grisly sexual mutilation.

An elderly farmer, Pietro Pacciani, was convicted two years ago of seven of the double murders but then dramatically cleared on appeal. The Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, overturned the appeal last month and ordered Pacciani's retrial.
The new request by Florence's public prosecutor Paolo Canessa stems from a continuing investigation into the murders.
Investigators allege Pacciani did not act alone in the last five double killings between 1981 and 1985 and that three of his associates took part in some or all of those murders.
A preliminary examining judge must review the bid to try the men for murder and other charges. No date for a committal hearing has been set yet.
One of the men named in the indictment request, Giancarlo Lotti, a labourer, has been providing information to investigators and is under police protection.
The other two defendants were Mario Vanni, held in jail since last February after Lotti's allegations that he had also taken part in the killings, and a third man, Giovanni Faggi.
